H1732: David, the youngest son of Jesse
H835: happiness; only in masculine plural construction as interjection, how happy!
H5375: to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative
H3680: properly, to plump, i.e. fill up hollows; by implication, to cover (for clothing or secrecy)
H2401: an offence, or a sacrifice forit
H120: ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.)
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H2803: properly, to plait or interpenetrate, i.e. (literally) to weave or (generally) to fabricate; figuratively, to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H369: a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle
H7307: wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension, a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit, but only of a rational being (including its expression and functions)
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H2790: to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to engrave, plough; hence (from the use of tools) to fabricate (of any material); figuratively, to devise (in a bad sense); hence (from the idea of secrecy) to be silent, to let alone; hence (by implication) to be deaf (as an accompaniment of dumbness)
H1086: to fail; by implication to wear out, decay (causatively, consume, spend)
H6106: a bone (as strong); by extension, the body; figuratively, the substance, i.e. (as pron.) selfsame
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H3117: a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb)
H3915: properly, a twist (away of the light), i.e. night; figuratively, adversity
H3513: to be heavy, i.e. in a bad sense (burdensome, severe, dull) or in a good sense (numerous, rich, honorable; causatively, to make weighty (in the same two senses)
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H3027: a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.),
H2015: to turn about or over; by implication, to change, overturn, return, pervert
H3955: (figuratively) vigor; also a sweet or fat cake
H7019: harvest (as the crop), whether the product (grain or fruit) or the (dry) season
H2403: an offence (sometimes habitual sinfulness), and its penalty, occasion, sacrifice, or expiation; also (concretely) an offender
H3045: to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
H3034: physically, to throw (a stone, an arrow) at or away; especially to revere or worship (with extended hands); intensively, to bemoan (by wringing the hands)
H859: thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
H6419: to judge (officially or mentally); by extension, to intercede, pray
H413: near, with or among; often in general, to
H6256: time, especially (adverb with preposition) now, when, etc.
H4672: properly, to come forth to, i.e. appear or exist; transitively, to attain, i.e. find or acquire; figuratively, to occur, meet or be present
H7535: properly, leanness, i.e. (figuratively) limitation; only adverbial, merely, or conjunctional, although
H4325: water; figuratively, juice; by euphemism, urine, semen
H7227: abundant (in quantity, size, age, number, rank, quality)
H5060: properly, to touch, i.e. lay the hand upon (for any purpose; euphemistically, to lie with a woman); by implication, to reach (figuratively, to arrive, acquire); violently, to strike (punish, defeat, destroy, etc.)
H5643: a cover (in a good or a bad, a literal or a figurative sense)
H6862: narrow; (as a noun) a tight place (usually figuratively, i.e. trouble); also a pebble ; (transitive) an opponent (as crowding)
H5341: to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.)
H5437: to revolve, surround, or border; used in various applications, literally and figuratively
H7919: to be (causatively, make or act) circumspect and hence, intelligent
H3384: properly, to flow as water (i.e. to rain); transitively, to lay or throw (especially an arrow, i.e. to shoot); figuratively, to point out (as if by aiming the finger), to teach
H1870: a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb
H3212: to walk (literally or figuratively); causatively, to carry (in various senses)
H3289: to advise; reflexively, to deliberate or resolve
H5869: an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape)
H408: not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing
H1961: to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
H5483: a horse (as leaping); also a swallow (from its rapid flight)
H6505: a mule (perhaps from his lonely habits)
H995: to separate mentally (or distinguish), i.e.(generally) understand
H7448: a halter (as restraining); by implication, the jaw
H5716: finery; generally an outfit; specifically, a headstall
H1077: properly, a failure; by implication nothing; usually (adverb) not at all; also lest
H7126: to approach (causatively, bring near) for whatever purpose
H7563: morally wrong; concretely, an (actively) bad person
H982: figuratively, to trust, be confident or sure
H2617: kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty
H8055: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
H1523: properly, to spin round (under the influence of any violent emotion), i.e. usually rejoice, or (as cringing) fear
H7442: properly, to creak (or emit a stridulous sound), i.e. to shout (usually for joy)
H3820: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
